# Agent Operating Guide (Project Map)
<!-- Generated by DevRails 26 init-mb.js. Safe to overwrite with init-mb.js --sync. -->

## Working approach

Follow `.memory-bank/workflows/execute-loop.md#working-policy`:
intent/requirements → features/design → tasks → implementation/checks → memory.
Combine stages and use existing results when sufficient. Skills support this
flow; they are not a mandatory sequence of approvals or separate sessions.

Consult the operator on unsettled substantive product, technical, and process
choices. Autopilot or an explicit instruction to work autonomously permits
choices inside the assigned objective and constraints. Already agreed work
needs no repeated approval. Explicit user directions can waive framework process
steps without exception paperwork; report any unperformed checks honestly.

## Context and roles

Read the context needed for the current outcome: the user's request, relevant
Constitution decisions, task/feature, and their linked requirements and specs.
Use `.memory-bank/index.md` and `spec-index.md` to locate missing context.
Do not load every Memory Bank document by default.

The default top-level role is GENERAL. Role guidance lives under
`.memory-bank/roles/`. A delegated assignment names its scope and expected result;
respect read-only and explicit write boundaries. Additional agents and fresh
contexts are useful when they reduce work or improve an important assessment,
not a prerequisite for ordinary progress.

## Creator Vibe Lens

Consider what the user is trying to make possible and what must remain theirs.
When success depends on taste, voice, or unstated intent, use the installed
`creator-vibe` skill. The lens never changes explicit instructions, facts,
permissions, or scope; mechanical work needs only accuracy and clarity.

## Reasoning Policy: Selection Before Expansion (KISS Gate)

Choose the simplest sufficient solution. Reuse or simplify before adding a new
mechanism. Additional abstractions, artifacts, checks, and processes need a
current requirement or evidenced material risk that justifies their cost.
A possible edge case is not a requirement. Report material, evidenced issues;
do not grow scope through speculative findings.

## Source path semantics

Preserve tooling conventions, public paths, exports, and executable identities.
Use descriptive names suited to the existing project. Rename files only when
needed for the requested outcome.

## Memory and execution

Keep Memory Bank maximally compact: only facts, accepted decisions and their
essential rationale, real open questions, and useful evidence or links. No filler,
rhetoric, repeated explanations, conversation transcripts, or empty template
sections. Link to canonical content instead of duplicating it. Every sentence
must help future work; preserve necessary meaning, not verbosity.

- `.memory-bank/` holds canonical project knowledge and indexed JSON tasks.
- `.tasks/` holds substantial execution artifacts when useful.
- `.protocols/` holds resumable task/run notes when needed; templates are aids.

Keep accepted requirements, specs, links, task state, and results consistent with
the work. Prefer updating an existing canonical source over copying it into a
report. Shared specs use subject-based paths; feature docs link to them.

Use the task schema and `TASK-NNN-TN-FT-NNN-WN` IDs consistently. Task
`touched_files` is advisory; a deliberately populated `write_boundary` and
explicit forbidden scope define permissions. Unmet real dependencies and
unresolved substantive decisions matter; absent reviews, formal approval markers,
or full protocols do not by themselves block execution.

Choose useful project-native checks and state their actual results. `/verify`,
`/red-verify`, and `/mb-doctor` are available when their assessment helps. Their
absence is not a reason to invent evidence or repeat completed work. Task/run
closure and recovery follow `.memory-bank/workflows/tier-policy.md` and
`autonomy-policy.md`.

## Communication

Answer in Russian, preserving conventional technical terms. Explain the result,
checks, limitations, and any decision needed in plain language. Avoid exposing
internal workflow vocabulary as a substitute for an explanation.
Do not generate slop: avoid generic platitudes, padding, and redundant summaries.

## Log papercuts

Record minor, evidenced project problems in one session file under
`PAPERCUTS/<model> __ MM-DD-YYYY HH.MM.md`, created only for the first finding.
Use local time and replace filename-unsafe model characters with `-`. Reuse the
file without timestamps inside it. For a project-wide problem that makes current
work unsafe or invalid, record it in ALL CAPS and stop the affected work.

## Where skills live

- Codex: `.agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`.
- Claude Code: `.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`.
- `.codex/` holds project configuration, not skills.

Follow the user's named skill or clear task directly. `/start` helps when the
next useful action is unclear. Commit or publish only within the user's granted
scope; ordinary implementation does not authorize unrelated external actions.
